findings.message: AC-4 limits 'shipped to Prod' to proposals that a Prod deployment released, and in-prod.ts claims to be the only In Prod rule. deliveryPerformance (068 AC-5, 'proposals shipped to Prod this month and last') still counts every row where phase = 'released' by released_at. That includes Released history brought in from the repo's archive (091 AC-4) and proposals whose only Prod deployment has been voided. Fix: add `and ${proposalInProd}` to its where clause, as shippedPerWeek and phaseCounts now do.
findings.scenario: A push from the default branch brings in an archived change (FLT-801) as Released history with released_at this month. The Proposals page's 'Released this month' stays at N, but the overview's delivery performance shows N+1 'shipped to Prod this month'.

findings.message: AC-1 is applied to SyncInput.createdAt and upsertSpecProposal, but the sync_proposal MCP tool's input schema has no createdAt and does not pass one to syncProposal. The same tool now takes task doneAt (TaskInput) and meta.repoPhases. Zod strips the key, so a credential or agent that syncs through sync_proposal cannot give the repo's created date, and the proposal is dated at the sync time. Fix: add `createdAt: repoTime` to the tool input and forward it.
findings.scenario: A service credential calls sync_proposal with createdAt '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' for a new change. The key is stripped, and created_at is now() (10 Nov) instead of 1 Oct.

findings.message: tickDates dates a task only from a commit whose diff removes `- [ ] `Tn`` and adds `- [x] `Tn``. When change.md first appears on the walked branch with its boxes already ticked, no commit has an open line to remove, so every task gets no doneAt. This happens with a squash-merged PR (the squash commit adds the folder) and with a change committed in one go. writeTasks then falls back to now(), even though git can tell the date: the commit that added the ticked line is when it was ticked on that branch. Fix: when the add commit, or the first commit that has a task's line, adds it already ticked, date the task by that commit. Add a table row for a change added with ticked tasks. The same code is in plugins/amax/scripts/read-specclaw.mjs.
findings.scenario: A repo that squash-merges: main gets one commit dated 2026-10-07 that adds 301-x/change.md with `- [x] `T1``. The first push from main stores T1.done_at as the sync time (2026-11-10), not 2026-10-07. repoDatesStale never corrects it because doneAt stays unknown.

findings.message: repoPhasesInMeta accepts a caller-supplied `{ at, source }` entry, and resolveRepoPhases keeps that source as the read that recorded the phase. Through sync_proposal, a caller can store any string as the read, and it does not have to match the write's meta.source. The history line then names a read that never happened. Fix: on input, accept only plain times per phase, and set the source from the write's meta.source. Keep stored entries' sources only from the locked row.
findings.scenario: sync_proposal with meta.source 'main@abc1234' and meta.repoPhases.verify = { at: '2026-10-07T10:00:00Z', source: 'main@deadbeef' } → the history line reads 'Verified in the repo · From the repo, read at main@deadbee'.
